title: Corruption and the Immutability of the Spirit
english: By this being corrupted, it is as if it were perishing, such as that which is called eternal losing out of itself, that is, being changed; it finds death, even if it remains otherwise, by its own alteration. For whatever you perceive to have happened later, this is the death of the former; it is like something such as evil happening, whereby goodness is killed by it, from which it departed, by the goodness; and the reverse, goodness by evil. For there is something which, though it must always stand by the first principle, even if it did not deny this to them, does not endure.

Indeed, Peter discusses these things in the epistles: 'If God did not spare the sinned angels, but cast them into Tartarus in chains of darkness, to be kept for judgment on the great day' (2 Peter 2:4), and 'he did not spare the ancient world' (2 Peter 2:5); and Jude: 'and angels who did not keep their own dominion, but left their own habitation, he has kept in chains of darkness under gloom to be judged on the great day' (Jude 1:6). And the rational material creation receives alteration: in one respect as Jude lost sanctification; and as Paul writes: 'the woman who lives in dissipation has been made dead, though she lives' (1 Timothy 5:5); even while enduring life in man. But in essence, it is as perishing first, and then falling into immortality. 'For it is necessary,' he says, 'that this corruptible put on incorruption, and this mortal put on immortality' (1 Corinthians 15:53). And the irrational creation undergoes a change and passes away: as it was foretold when light turns into darkness and water into blood: 'this is the alteration of the right hand of the Most High'; and elsewhere: 'the heaven,' he says, 'and the earth will pass away' (Matthew 24:35). For it was foretold that there would be new heavens and a new earth. For everything that received a beginning truly has also an end.

But the Holy Spirit, being of that unspeakable and all-prevailing eternal and incorruptible nature, and always having [it] in the same way and according to the same things; only as a mode and performing the things of God; and being a guardian of all, both the rational and perfecting the faith of the irrational, and of the irrational, until the condition of abiding in identity was given to the irrational; has been made unfit for a change of nature and a change of will, which is incorruptible. For the unshakeable is indeed incorruptible, and immediately it is without beginning, without end, and surpassing eternity. And the one without beginning:
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Error of Heretics Regarding Eternity and the Spirit
english: Regarding the phrase 'unto the ages of ages.' It is not possible to hear it as it is, for those who are divided concerning the theologies of the Holy Spirit have determined this as a main point. For they lead themselves to the ends of the earth by presumption; and unmeasured passion is not accustomed to testify accurately to an investigation; nevertheless, nothing prevents one from hearing that device of theirs. For if they could, they would make it even more widely known.

Thus it is here: if something is called 'eternal' by name, it is possible to call it God, but if it is merely 'everlasting,' it is the Creator of the ages. For it is written: 'God is the maker of times and ages' (Ps 90:2), and again: 'Of old God spoke in many ways and in many manners to the prophets, but at the end of the days He spoke to us in Son, whom He set as heir of all things, through whom also He made the ages' (Heb 1:1-2). For if everything called 'eternal' must be named God, there would be infinite gods. For it is written: 'Rise up, eternal gates' (Ps 24:7), and again: 'Everlasting years were remembered' (Ps 102:17), and again: 'Like everlasting sheep' (Isa 54:13), and: 'These shall rise to eternal punishment' (Matt 25:46), and elsewhere: 'Those in the dust of the earth shall rise, some to everlasting life, and others to everlasting shame' (John 5:29).

Is then both the punishment and the shame God? See how much absurdity and impiety the shared name of 'eternal' falls into; it leaps upon and is swept along by the meanings and words of those people; but this is dissolved by these things: regarding the eternal name, as we have just remembered, the others, whatever they may be, did not come from time alone; but they also have the corruption of the nature of opinion, and their 'everlastingness' is altogether unlike the divine eternity; just as the one called holy, angel, or man, is similarly and perhaps this is to the Holy of Holies Spirit; for in the whole, holiness and eternity exist.

Pay attention, then, to what great clamor the 'eternal' is raised concerning the Holy Spirit, and that this wonderful and most uncontainable thing has been applied to Him, I say that He who through the Holy Spirit made the ages brings Himself to His own true Father on our behalf. Let them also consider that all the powers of the heavens are in the Holy Spirit, certainly as a co-worker with the ungraspable Creator; and that,

The heretics, not at an opportune time but in confusion, mentioned the eternal gates and thresholds, having said these things as a summary of what was brought forward to us in words. Let the difference be clear to them between the unoriginated and unchangeable eternal, and that which is from time and subject to change, and let it be known that this is not brief, nor is it only another beauty regarding essence, but is altogether transformed. Let it also be known that the Holy Spirit holds the eternal judgment toward God the Father, who strengthens all things, and the Son, not toward creatures. Having released the inferior opinion, let them embrace the better; and let them marvel, instead of what they do now, at what is worthy of marveling; and let them practice a better time after these things, for there is no envy. And having made themselves victims of the arrogant reproach of those things, they have thereby brought forth the benefit of repentance.

For if this word, as something indicating the divine, was used concerning God the Father and the Son, perhaps it might similarly be applied to the Spirit of God. One thing is this: another is that nothing of those things of which they remembered the eternal was decreed as divine, or a Holy Spirit proceeding from God—that is, one thing, and not a plurality; nor is it arranged with the Father and the Son for divine initiation and divine gift, nor of any other, lest I say too much, it was unworthy of the honor belonging to divinity. Other things toward this: God and Father pleased through His Son, the Word, to have all things created. And what an insult, as they dream, to His all-holy Spirit, from not being created! For if, according to them, it is not inexpressibly a co-worker with the Creator as the Father is? But since all energy and gift, creative and good and perfect, belongs to His only-begotten Son, the Word, and to the one Holy Spirit, and is common to them, all things are led up to the One, from whom these blessed hypotheses appeared inexpressibly along with Him; these things a person, having made himself a quiet examiner, full of the reasonings of wisdom, which are mentioned in various places of this book and those before it, could easily learn. And Paul, who is greater than men, left this clearly confirmed to the Corinthians: 'But you were removed, but you were justified, but...'
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Nature of Creation and the Holy Spirit
english: “You were baptized in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ and in the spirit of our God.” Therefore, look, look, how the name of the Son is entirely a divine name, and likewise that of the Holy Spirit; for one name has revealed both of them. And that the Holy Spirit, as if having gathered them ineffably from the beginning, now recreates. For to have loosed [the old] signified to be recreated. By this title: “having regenerated us through the bath of regeneration and the renewal of the Holy Spirit” (Titus 3:5). The Psalmist is no less worthy of being known regarding those already existing in generation who are now being created in the divine swimming pool spiritually. For he says: “A people being created [praises] the Lord” (Psalm 50:2).

Do not then the hypostases, which possess the same honor and energy, inherit the same nature, and do not differ from one another in deity and power, but alone are able to be infused, arranged, and everywhere co-thought with the One; who is both of them, not from where the hypostases are for both, but has from himself, uncountably, and equally and similarly, the hypostases united and continuous. Furthermore, regarding what has been said: every decree of these heretics is similarly, as also similarly-spoken, of their currently moving error of sophistry, as we shall learn soon from their own chapters. For if by chance they say a certain word, such as “eternal” or “good”, bringing a divine indication concerning the Trinity in unity, and fitting to it entirely and perfectly, it happened to be said concerning a creature, along with the due memory of the creature, they say nothing, for what do they have to say? Concerning God the Father and his Son; but they immediately and thoughtlessly bring the Holy Spirit down to the creature, not appropriately leading up to God and the Only-begotten, those who, being most harmonious with the Holy Spirit in the same and equal [nature], have been unutterably described by the theologians. Therefore, only regarding those in the chapter in which we are proceeding, having been justified as unable to exceed, but sufficient for the whole struggle concerning the heretics: or let them show, which is very heavy to say, whether the beginning or the end of the Holy Spirit has perhaps been used; or entirely, that he had a certain way toward corruption, like the angelic and human choice; or let it be to them...

That which is called, 'an ox on the tongue.' I have said much regarding those things, but I will move to the initial hypothesis: that as it is unchangeable and incapable of virtue or vice, so the rational creation is capable of both virtue and vice, as we find in incorporeal beings—as we previously said, virtue is within the blessed angels, while vice is in the rejected ones; and in bodies, as we ourselves are.

But the divine Spirit, participating in virtue and glory, rather being the very source of the highest virtue, is incapable of either of these, just as neither the Father nor the Son is. And if it is incapable, it is also not of a different substance; for if it does everything the Father wills, it is not of a different substance. From this, therefore, it is gathered to know that it is not a creation, yet it stands in the same relation to God the Father, His Son, and the God who is from Him, from whom it naturally proceeded, as it is written: 'in us' (1 Cor 6:19).

That creation is sanctified and justified by Him who is the Holy God by nature; for it is capable of being sanctified and justified, not incapable. As for the Holy Spirit, since He is distinguished—being separate from creation but joined to that nature from which He proceeded, concerning which we have been initiated, saying: 'Every good gift and every perfect gift is from above, coming down from the Father of lights, with whom there is no variation or shadow of turning' (James 1:17)—and since He cares for and provides for even the lowly: He sanctifies, justifies, and grants wisdom, and provides every kind of heavenly virtue; but He is by no means found to have a need to be sanctified, justified, or made wise by another, just as neither the self-existent Father nor His consubstantial Son is.

For this reason, it is rightly called both 'Holy' and 'Spirit of Holiness', instead of 'holy by nature and from himself'; and 'Divine Spirit', instead of 'God by nature'; and 'Breath of the Almighty', instead of 'consubstantial with the Almighty, breathed from His person'; so that He alone shows such a name, being consubstantial with God the Father, sanctifying, and not even being contained by the Word. For Paul is able to both speak and set forth the patterns of faith.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
